Summary: DeepMind was founded by Demis Hassabis, Shane Legg, and Mustafa Suleyman in November 2010. The company was acquired by Google in 2014 for £400 million ($500 million) and later merged with Google AI's Google Brain division to become Google DeepMind in April 2023. The founders aimed to create a general-purpose AI that could be useful and effective for almost anything.

Summary: Google acquired DeepMind in 2014 for around $600 million, with sources indicating the amount was over $500 million. Business Insider and CNBC both mention the acquisition price being over $500 million, while TechCrunch reports the acquisition price was more than $500 million. The Robot Report specifies the acquisition amount as $643 million. Despite these variations, the consensus among the sources is that Google paid a substantial sum, upwards of $500 million, for DeepMind.

[1] Google's $500+ Million Acquisition of DeepMind Is Looking Good - Business Insider
    http://www.businessinsider.com/googles-400-million-acquisition-of-deepmind-is-looking-good-2016-7
    Google forked out over $500 million for a little-known London startup called DeepMind in 2014 without specifying how the company's artificial-intelligence technology would be used to increase Google's revenues, which already run into tens of billions of dollars every year.

That all changed on Wednesday when DeepMind announced that Google had found a use for DeepMind's technology in its enormous data centers. [...] The company has also said in the past couple of months that it intends to sell its products and services to healthcare providers like the NHS at some point, providing Google with an additional revenue stream.

All of this adds up to make DeepMind an interesting acquisition that could create significantly more than the $500 million Google paid for the startup. [...] DeepMind's technology has been deployed across only a handful of Google's data centers, but Google is planning to introduce the company's machine-learning software to all 15 of its data centers by the end of the year, potentially resulting in massive energy savings on Google's sizable electricity bill.

observations.content:
Summary: The founders of DeepMind are Demis Hassabis, Shane Legg, and Mustafa Suleyman. The company was established in 2010 with the mission to develop artificial general intelligence (AGI) and has since made significant contributions to AI, including breakthroughs like AlphaGo and AlphaFold. Hassabis, who has a background in cognitive neuroscience and video game design, served as CEO until 2026 when he became Alphabet's chief scientist. Suleyman, who met Hassabis as teenagers, has since moved on to other ventures, including co-founding Inflection AI.

[1] Demis Hassabis: Co-Founder and CEO of DeepMind (now Google DeepMind) – ETEC522: The Innovative Educator
    https://blogs.ubc.ca/etec522/2026/06/08/demis-hassabis-co-founder-and-ceo-of-deepmind-now-google-deepmind
    Google DeepMind is an artificial intelligence research company founded in 2010 by Demis Hassabis, Shane Legg, and Mustafa Suleyman. The company’s mission is to develop artificial general intelligence (AGI) that can advance scientific discovery and solve complex global challenges. DeepMind is known for breakthroughs such as AlphaGo, AlphaFold, and Gemini, as well as its contributions to healthcare, scientific research, and artificial intelligence development (Google DeepMind, n.d.-a). Its [...] Image source: The Economist (2026).

## Venture: Google DeepMind [...] ## Founder Analysis

Demis Hassabis represents an unusual combination of scientist, entrepreneur, and lifelong learner. Before founding DeepMind, he was a child chess prodigy, a successful video game designer, and later earned a PhD in cognitive neuroscience (Google DeepMind, n.d.-b; The Nobel Prize, 2024). This interdisciplinary background appears to have shaped his vision of building AI by studying how humans learn and think.

[2] Google DeepMind Enters a New Era: Where Are Its 3 Founders Now? | Observer
    https://observer.com/2026/09/google-deepmind-cofounders-ai-leadership
    Long before it became an A.I. powerhouse, Google DeepMind was simply DeepMind. Founded in London by machine learning researchers Demis Hassabis, Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman, the lab was launched with the goal of achieving artificial general intelligence (AGI). Hassabis and Suleyman met as teenagers in London, while Hassabis later met Legg at University College London’s Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit.
